items.title: Does Multi-Agent Debate Improve AI Feedback on Research Papers?
items.desc: In a pre-registered, identity-masked experiment, authors of 44 economics meta-analyses ranked AI reports on their own papers; multi-agent debate tools did not beat a single frontier-model pass, questioning the value of agentic debate for research feedback. [arXiv econ.GN, posted 2026-07-16]

items.title: When Is Delegated Play Truthful? Within-Range Regret and the Trilemma of Aligned Delegation
items.desc: Studies when it is optimal to honestly describe one's goals to an automated proxy that acts on your behalf in a mechanism (autobidders, LLM agents), formalizing a trilemma of aligned delegation via a within-range regret criterion. [arXiv econ.TH, posted 2026-07-15]

items.title: Tabular Foundation Models for Discrete Choice Estimation
items.desc: Tests whether tabular foundation models can do discrete-choice demand estimation via in-context learning; naive application underperforms, and the paper examines how to close the gap for this central marketing/operations framework. [arXiv econ.EM, posted 2026-07-14]

items.title: Governing Artificial Intelligence: Public Preferences and Regulatory Options
items.desc: Uses public-preference evidence to map how AI should be regulated, laying out the trade-offs policymakers face between innovation and safety and between public oversight and private self-regulation. [arXiv econ.GN, posted 2026-07-16]

items.title: Supervised Fine-Tuning vs. In-Context Learning: An Equilibrium Analysis of LLM Personalization under Congestion
items.desc: A game-theoretic model of when users should invest in costly supervised fine-tuning versus lightweight in-context learning for LLMs, and how congestion from other users' personalization reshapes those incentives. [arXiv econ.TH, posted 2026-07-15]

items.title: Equilibrium Information Aggregation under Machine Learning
items.desc: Studies the equilibrium effects when agents process information with a machine-learning procedure (a Chow-Liu tree); in an asset market with dispersed information, prices fail to aggregate what the algorithm extracts. [arXiv econ.TH, posted 2026-07-15]

items.title: Forecasting Inflation with Microdata: An Adaptive Machine Learning Approach
items.desc: Develops a scan test and an adaptive machine-learning pipeline that encodes the distribution of individual price changes to forecast aggregate inflation in non-stationary environments. [arXiv econ.GN, posted 2026-07-14]

items.title: Indirect Variational Inference: Applications to Earnings Dynamics
items.desc: Adapts variational inference from machine learning to estimate intractable latent-variable economic models, with an application to earnings dynamics and stronger parameter-recovery guarantees. [arXiv econ.GN, posted 2026-07-16]

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Finance: What Have We Learned?
items.desc: A bibliometric and multi-method topic-modelling review of the AI-in-finance literature (1,579 articles, 2012-2025) using LDA, BERTopic and Bunka; documents rapid US- and China-led growth around machine learning, FinTech, sustainability and LLMs. [SSRN, posted 2026-07-14]

items.title: SciPhy Reinforcement Learning for Portfolio Optimization
items.desc: Introduces a Scientific Physics-Informed Reinforcement Learning framework for dynamic portfolio optimization by large institutional investors, learning cost-aware, distribution-aware strategies from offline historical data in continuous time. [arXiv q-fin.PM, posted 2026-07-16]

items.title: Measuring Sentiment News with Transformer-Based Language Models
items.desc: Builds daily financial-news sentiment indicators using transformer-based language models that capture context, negation and semantic structure better than traditional dictionary word-count methods. [arXiv q-fin.GN, posted 2026-07-15]

items.title: VAIOM: Continuous-Input, Discrete-Output Decoder-Only Financial Sequence Modeling
items.desc: A decoder-only Transformer for probabilistic next-return prediction that ingests continuous, noisy financial observations and emits discrete ordinal-return distributions. [arXiv q-fin, posted 2026-07-15]

items.title: Is Deep Hedging Reinforcement Learning?
items.desc: Examines whether the deep-hedging framework, which trains a neural-network policy to minimize terminal hedging error, should be understood as reinforcement learning, clarifying the link between the two. [arXiv q-fin, posted 2026-07-15]

items.title: A Noise-Robust Elicit-to-Optimize Framework for Distortion Riskmetrics via Inverse Reinforcement Learning
items.desc: Combines inverse reinforcement learning and reinforcement learning to elicit agents' risk preferences and optimize policies under a broad class of distortion risk measures, robustly to noise. [arXiv q-fin.RM, posted 2026-07-15]

items.title: Diachronic Sample Integration: Robust Tail-Risk Estimation with Generative Models
items.desc: Improves deep generative models used as simulators for risk-sensitive decisions by concentrating on rare adverse scenarios, sharpening tail-risk estimation under data scarcity. [arXiv q-fin.RM, posted 2026-07-12]

items.title: Reinforcement Learning for Execution under Dynamic Fees in a Closed-Loop DEX Simulator
items.desc: Builds a closed-loop simulator of a decentralized exchange and uses reinforcement learning to study optimal trade execution when automated market makers charge trader-facing dynamic fees. [arXiv q-fin.CP, posted 2026-07-12]

sections.name: 📦 Operations & Supply Chain (INFORMS: Management Science, M&SOM, Operations Research)

items.title: Assortment Optimization Under the Decision Forest Model
items.desc: Optimizes assortments under the decision forest model — a nonparametric, tree-ensemble choice model that can represent nonrational customer behavior — letting firms tailor offerings to profitably exploit those deviations. [M&SOM, published online 2026-07-15]

items.title: Convex Surrogate Loss Functions for Contextual Pricing with Transaction Data
items.desc: Tackles off-policy contextual pricing from transaction data (past prices offered, purchase outcomes, customer/item features) by introducing convex surrogate loss functions to learn pricing policies without observing willingness-to-pay. [Management Science, published online 2026-07-14]

items.title: Scalable Bundle Recommendations: A Large-Scale Field Experiment
items.desc: An end-to-end, scalable machine-learning framework that builds product embeddings from clickstream data to design complementary/substitutable bundle recommendations, validated in a large field experiment across 4,500 products. [Management Science, published online 2026-07-15]

items.title: Nearly 200 Economists and Tech Leaders Warn of A.I. Threats
items.desc: Nearly 200 economists and technology leaders signed a warning about AI's risks to jobs and the economy, sharpening the debate over how fast automation could displace workers. [NYT, 2026-07-13]

items.title: Anthropic Inches Toward a Mega-I.P.O.
items.desc: Reporting on AI developer Anthropic moving toward a potential large initial public offering, a signal of how AI valuations are reshaping capital markets. [NYT DealBook, 2026-07-16]

items.title: Google Ordered to Give A.I. Rivals More Access on Android Smartphones
items.desc: A ruling requires Google to open more access to AI competitors on Android, an antitrust move with implications for competition in the AI economy. [NYT, 2026-07-16]

items.title: Is IBM a Canary in the Tech Coal Mine?
items.desc: Analyzes what IBM's AI software and consulting results signal about enterprise AI demand and the broader tech-spending economy. [NYT DealBook, 2026-07-15]

items.title: Chai Discovery, an A.I. Drug Start-Up, Raises $400 Million
items.desc: AI drug-discovery start-up Chai Discovery raised $400 million, underscoring continued heavy venture financing flowing into applied-AI companies. [NYT DealBook, 2026-07-14]

items.title: OpenAI Is Showing Kalshi's World Cup Odds in ChatGPT
items.desc: OpenAI is surfacing prediction-market odds from Kalshi inside ChatGPT, an early tie-up between a leading AI platform and financial-style event markets. [NYT, 2026-07-13]

items.title: The Hottest AI Models in Silicon Valley Face a Powerful Source of Competition
items.desc: Leading Silicon Valley AI model developers, squeezed by rising costs, are facing a powerful new source of competition — a shift with real implications for the economics of the AI-model business. [Washington Post, 2026-07-14]

items.title: New York Becomes First State to Impose Data Center Moratorium
items.desc: New York's governor signed an order making it the first state to halt new data centers, a move with major implications for the AI compute buildout and its energy and economic footprint. [Washington Post, 2026-07-14]

items.title: Sovereign AI, Independent of America and China, Is a Pipe Dream
items.desc: Argues that ambitions for 'sovereign AI' independent of American and Chinese technology are unrealistic given how concentrated compute, chips and model supply chains remain. [The Economist, 2026-07-16]

items.title: How Europe Can Compete on AI
items.desc: An Economist podcast on how Europe might build competitive AI capacity despite trailing the US and China in compute, capital and talent. [The Economist, 2026-07-15]

items.title: How to Make AI Safe—and Lessen Dependence on America and China
items.desc: An Economist leader arguing for policies that make AI safer while reducing other economies' dependence on American and Chinese AI models, chips and compute. [The Economist, 2026-07-15]

items.title: Demis Hassabis Has a Plan to Harness AI Safely
items.desc: An Economist business profile of DeepMind chief Demis Hassabis and his approach to developing and commercializing AI safely. [The Economist, 2026-07-14]
